venue_analysis.downtown_linden_corner: Cafe, $. Fully meat-free board, light and fresh, peanut-allergic diner eats the whole menu safely, oat milk by default, olive oil instead of butter, bean-thickened soup. Meets every constraint: 3 stars.

venue_analysis.downtown_marble_steps: Vegan-style, nut-safe and dairy-free, but heavy fried food. Misses Brooke's wholesome request: 2 stars.

notes: Each constraint gets its own clean decoy: Slate Window fails only on peanuts, Wren House only on meat, Paper Kite only on dairy, Marble Steps only on 'wholesome'. That is good design. Linden Corner is the only venue that clears everything.
The peanut allergy is implied ('emergency pen', 'satay'), and Roxy's 'nothing satay-adjacent' line confirms it. Fair, and it rewards close reading.

Mina's vegetarianism is only implied through the sushi-day memory ('zero meat', 'order without asking'). A careful player gets it, but it reads more like a fond preference than a strict diet. A player who scores it as a preference would still pick Linden Corner, since Wren House also has nothing else going for it beyond -1. Consider one slightly firmer hint if it is meant as a strict diet.
No budget is given in the chat. It does not matter because every venue is $.

Linden Corner's reviews are noticeably long and spell out every constraint (meat-free, peanut-allergic deskmate, oat latte, olive oil, light food). That makes the answer a little obvious once the constraints are found. Slate Window's 'every grain bowl comes coated with satay dressing' is similarly blunt.
